svg.text: The arithmetic heart of the 3D counterexample: the last nonzero digit
Toy prime p = 5 (the paper needs p > 200). f(m) = last nonzero base-p digit of m, f(0) = 1.
A. f(m) for m = 0..624, read in rows of 25
Columns 5k replay it at the next digit. Each zoom by
p reveals the same sequence again, so no period fits.
B. No vertical period: every shift M fails somewhere
first m with f(m + M) ≠ f(m)
Checked by brute force for every M from 1 to 624
Mechanism (paper, Section 2): a period must be divisible
by p; then W(n, pm) is again a solution with period M/p.
Infinite descent: no positive period survives.
C. The line rule: every slanted line reads an allowed word
Unmarked cells: word = an + b mod p. ●: p | an + b, word = (an + b)/p
mod p. ○: p² | an + b, value unrestricted.
Brute force over all witnesses (a, b) mod 25: all 625 lines with
|d|, |e| ≤ 12 are allowed; a perturbed word is rejected.
Illustration only: the paper encodes this rule (p > 200, N = p² columns) into one finite tile of ℤ² × ℤ/Q, then rigidifies it into ℤ³.
The actual tile is far too large to draw; this picture shows the arithmetic reason its tilings cannot be periodic.
